packages/troupe-identity-local/tests/tes: The default identity chain with the filesystem adapter, which has no VCS identity, so the OS login is used (spec: identity).
packages/troupe-store-text/tests/test_pr: Reading a child writer's outcome from its standard output (its last line, after nothing but lock-wait announcements, or the test fails naming the line), and a store seeing an event that another store on the same theatre recorded while its watch was being set up, at once and without falling back to polling (spec: event-store, "Writers wait for each other, bounded and announced" and "A subscription delivers other writers' events as they're recorded"; design D10).
packages/troupe-store-text/tests/test_sh: Several stores on one theatre, in one process (spec: event-store, "Notification IDs are local, dense and never renumbered" and "Followers' positions are local"; troupe-run/troupe#450). Each store keeps the local order and tracking logs in memory, and these tests check that a store sees what another store wrote to them before it relies on its own copy, so no notification id is appended twice and no follower's position goes backwards. They also check that an order, tracking or issued file that is repeated, conflicting, damaged, shortened or deleted is repaired, rebuilt under a new epoch, or refused.

A store records events after another process has recorded to the same theatre, and gives them notification ids after that process's ones without reusing any (spec: event-store, "Notification IDs are local, dense and never renumbered"; troupe-run/troupe#450).
packages/troupe-vcs-git/tests/test_git_a: Narrowing the git adapter's environment policy to names outside it is refused as environment.policy-invalid (spec: vcs; event-store design D11).
packages/troupe/tests/test_anthropic_hos: Checks that the test limits the Anthropic stand-in service, the plugin's harness and the live tests each hold are the same (spec: anthropic-runner; anthropic-runner design D14).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_changes_u: Writing troupe diff's output to a byte stream passes the captured bytes through unchanged, adding no newline and translating no line ending (spec: cli, run-workspaces; worktree-stage design D6).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_config_pa: A config change entry or conflict at a key that holds a dot is shown with that key in brackets, the form it is typed in (spec: config, "A config path is shown in the form it is typed"; config-path-dotted-keys design D3, D4).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_config_un: The config command group on the command line: config with no command is refused naming the commands it takes, and a flag a config command doesn't take is refused as an unknown flag (spec: cli, config; config-model design D10).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_init_unit: troupe init writes its printed steps for PowerShell on Windows and for a POSIX shell everywhere else (spec: cli; init-and-audition design D4, D8, D9).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_integrati: The installed troupe console script, run as its own process from a directory with no theatre, prints the installed version, writes nothing to standard error and creates no theatre (spec: cli).
packages/troupe/tests/test_cli_startup_u: The client dispatcher's table names exactly the methods its command families offer, and an unknown method is refused listing every method troupe offers (spec: cli; cli-starts-fast design D6).
packages/troupe/tests/test_config_abando: The keep record of abandoned config edits: no record means none kept, an unreadable record counts as none and is named in a notice, and keeping twice records one entry and prunes changes that are gone (spec: config-hand-edits; abandoned-edits design D7).
packages/troupe/tests/test_config_change: Config's change entries: each value's old hash and new value, groups removed and set whole, renames, and a path changed twice in one command recorded as its net change (spec: config; config-model design D2).

Config's changes recorded in a real theatre: a command setting two values records one event with an entry for each, two commands record two events with their own change ids, and the config stream has the same id in every theatre (spec: config; config-model design D2).
packages/troupe/tests/test_config_files_: Config's files in a real git theatre: a clean merge of two branches is left as it is, conflict markers typed by hand are refused, a flush waits for another process writing config and says so, and troupe's git attribute keeps a file's line endings under autocrlf (spec: config-files; config-model design D7, D8, D9).
packages/troupe/tests/test_config_schema: Config's generated models are what its schemas generate: a schema changed without its models fails the check naming the fix, and regenerating writes models the check then accepts (spec: config; config-model design D2, D6, D11).
packages/troupe/tests/test_event_payload: The event payload schemas, checked against payloads built in each test: a Run.Ended payload validates only when its ending, audit, transcript and transcript format agree, a Run.Noticed payload only when it holds one declared notice, and an end's recording only when it names a run event or a notice. Also checks that the topics troupe records are the topics the event-record schema defines, that each payload schema's title names its topic, and that an ended run's error refers to the error catalogue (spec: event-store; strict-schemas design D6).
packages/troupe/tests/test_openai_host_u: Checks that the test limits the OpenAI stand-in service, the plugin's harness and the live tests each hold are the same (spec: openai-runner; openai-style-runner design D13).
packages/troupe/tests/test_perform_runti: perform's refusal of an Anthropic runtime whose endpoint from config ends in /v1 names the base to use and the config path the endpoint came from (spec: runtimes, "An Anthropic actor on an endpoint ending in /v1"; runtimes design D5, D6, D8).
packages/troupe/tests/test_platform_watc: Watching a directory, with every change made in this process (platform/watching.py; spec: platform; watch-event-segments design D2, D7). A wait with nothing changing returns after its timeout, even when the platform gives up early, closing a watch wakes a wait in another thread at once, and removing the watched directory wakes a wait and the next one names it missing. Watching a missing directory, a file, or a directory the OS call refuses fails naming the directory and the reason.
packages/troupe/tests/test_run_changes_u: A run summary's changes must fit where the run worked: a run in the theatre that has changes, and pending changes without a diff, are refused by the schema and by the client message classes (spec: run-workspaces; worktree-stage design D6; account-for-every-worktree design D5, D6).
packages/troupe/tests/test_run_host_unit: Tests for the run host that need no running runner: a runner command that doesn't exist could not start and has no audit, a masked transcript record is framed so it validates and decodes to the masked bytes, and every valid runner line is read with no kept string holding the credential, while keys that masking would merge are a protocol violation (spec: actor-runners, runner-protocol).
packages/troupe/tests/test_runner_confor: How the conformance suite reads the runner it checks from the environment: TROUPE_CONFORMANCE_RUNNER as a JSON array command line, TROUPE_CONFORMANCE_OPTIONS as JSON run/start options, and TROUPE_CONFORMANCE_RUNTIME as a JSON object resolved as a run resolves a runtime, whose credential is named only by the variable that holds it and reaches the runner as TROUPE_RUNTIME_CREDENTIAL. Unset or empty means absent, and anything else malformed is refused, naming the variable and never repeating a key (spec: actor-runners; conformance-runtime design D1-D3).
packages/troupe/tests/test_runner_warm_u: Which runners warm their engine, and how it's announced: a runner without a warm-up starts no process, only the mistralrs runner has one (its --warm-up argument), and a runner.warming-up notice naming the runner comes before it starts (spec: cli; in-process-runner design D4; owner, 2026-11-14).
packages/troupe/tests/test_schemas_integ: A runner's options schema is read from the installed runner's published files without importing the runner, checked in a fresh interpreter (spec: protocol, scripted-runner; config-model design D13, D17).
plugins/runner-anthropic/tests/test_anth: The fixtures, read from their files: every fixture the spec names is there, each says where it came from and which engine counted it, the named cases expect the outcome the spec gives them, and none holds a key, a request id, an account or a home directory (spec: anthropic-runner, "Fixtures pair service output with protocol events", "Fixtures hold no secrets", "Fixtures that need a working credential are captured by the owner"; design D12, D14).

Each fixture replays through the fake endpoint and the real runner to the events it expects, and the runner writes no part of the credential (spec: anthropic-runner, "Fixtures pair service output with protocol events"; design D12, D14).
How the runner writes a message: a lone surrogate in it is written as U+FFFD, and the runner says on standard error how many it replaced (spec: anthropic-runner; host-robustness design D3).

The one module that uses the anthropic package, against the fake Messages API (spec: anthropic-runner, "The library finds nothing of its own", "The credential goes only in the Authorization header", "Redirects are never followed", "Every timeout the library applies is one of the runner's named settings"; design D4, D10).

Where it's cheap, each guarantee is also shown failing for the library's own default client, so a test here fails if the runner's setting is lost rather than passing because the library happened to behave.

How the module that uses the anthropic package keeps the library's own logging out of the run's output: a debug record asked for reaches neither standard output nor standard error, and a warning reaches the runner's stream as one line, masked and cut (spec: anthropic-runner, "The library's own logging stays out of the run's output").
plugins/runner-claude-code/tests/test_cl: The capture tool's stand-in Messages API, over a local socket: the compaction stand-in answers a read, then the summary, then done, counting one compaction, and the reactive stand-in refuses the second ordinary request and counts the refusal (spec: claude-code-runner; compaction-off design D3; compaction-opt-in design D10).

Declaring a delete effect builds Claude Code's command line with an MCP config naming troupe's effects server, passed with --strict-mcp-config, and allows its Delete tool in the settings (spec: claude-code-runner, "Delete and move effects are troupe's own tools"; declared-effects design D8).

The harness's check for a stand-in claude left running, which passes when no record was written and fails naming a record that names no pid, and how the runner writes a message: a lone surrogate in it is written as U+FFFD, with the count on standard error (spec: claude-code-runner; host-robustness design D3).
plugins/runner-mistralrs/tests/test_mist: The check model the plugin carries is the file its provenance records, under the two MIT licences it records (spec: mistralrs-runner, "Tests load no downloaded model"; in-process-runner design D10; owner, 2026-11-14: check and record its MIT licence).

The built wheel carries the check model, its provenance and its licence (spec: mistralrs-runner, "Tests load no downloaded model"; in-process-runner design D10; owner, 2026-11-14: check and record its MIT licence).
plugins/runner-ollama/tests/test_ollama_: The capture tool refuses an endpoint that isn't on this machine, and the replay starts each fixture with the files its capture made (local-model-runner design D12).

Closing the Ollama client shuts down the socket that TLS moved a connection onto, not only the first one, checked with local socket pairs standing in for the connection (ollama-library design D4, D8).

The Ollama client's address check and error text: a bracketed host that isn't an IPv6 address is unreachable rather than a crash, and an error's text is its status followed by Ollama's message or the body (spec: ollama-runner; local-model-runner design D9).

Helpers of the conversation's tool loop: the tool limits follow the context window and never pass the SDK's defaults, encode writes compact UTF-8, and fit_output keeps a tool's output within a budget smaller than its note (spec: ollama-runner; local-model-runner design D15).
The fake Ollama's done line holds a cached prompt count only when a test gives one, so the runner's tests can trust it (local-model-runner design D12).

The Ollama fixtures, read from their files: there is one for each shape, each named case holds what Ollama sent and the outcome it should give, each records its Ollama version, model, date and how it was made, and none holds a secret or a host path (spec: ollama-runner, "Fixtures pair real Ollama output with protocol events"; local-model-runner design D12).

Each Ollama fixture replayed through the runner gives exactly the records and events it holds, and a fixture whose run the preflight refuses is refused with its code (spec: ollama-runner, "Fixtures pair real Ollama output with protocol events"; local-model-runner design D12).

The Ollama runner driven in this process over in-memory streams: a failure of the runner itself is reported, and the runner answers and exits 1, also when its input ends after the failure, and a lone surrogate in a message is written as U+FFFD with the count on standard error (spec: ollama-runner, runner-protocol; host-robustness design D3).
plugins/runner-openai/tests/test_openai_: The capture tool sends nothing to a proxy for an endpoint on this machine, even with a proxy set in the environment (spec: openai-runner; design D13). It's loaded by path, as the owner runs it.

Parts of one exchange with the service: Retry-After is read as seconds or as an HTTP date, a response's events are closed when the attempt ends rather than when they're collected, and a 401 whose body never ends, answered by an httpx2 mock transport, is read only to the body limit and ends as an authentication failure without a retry (spec: openai-runner, "A rate limit's Retry-After is honoured within a named cap", "Failures retrying can't fix end the run at once", "A body read whole stops at a named limit", "An error that never ends").

The fake endpoint's pause, timed on its own with no request served, lasts its length even by a monotonic clock as coarse as Windows' on Python 3.12 (openai-style-runner design D13). The runner's own tests rely on it.

The fixtures, read from their files: every required fixture is there, each says where it came from, the compacted and exhausted cases expect the outcome the spec gives them, the rejected-credential fixture used no working credential, and none holds a key, an account id or a home directory (spec: openai-runner, "Fixtures pair service output with protocol events", "Fixtures hold no secrets", "Failure fixtures are captured without a real credential"; design D13).

Each fixture replays through the fake endpoint and the real runner to the events it expects, and the runner writes no part of the credential (spec: openai-runner, "Fixtures pair service output with protocol events", "The credential goes only in the Authorization header"; design D13).

What the runner sets around the openai package (openai-library design D11): every variable the library reads is removed from the environment and nothing else, the library's warnings reach standard error masked and cut with nothing below a warning, and a status failure keeps its headers by lower-case name (spec: openai-runner, "The library finds nothing of its own", "The library's own logging stays out of the run's output").

The test harness refuses a run started on the real use limits unless a test gives its reason (design D7), and the runner writes a lone surrogate in a message as U+FFFD, with the count on standard error (spec: openai-runner; host-robustness design D3).

How the runner reaches a service through the openai package, checked in this process: which endpoints count as this machine, a credential over plain HTTP to another host refused, where requests go and through which proxy, the library's timeouts, and the caps on a stream's lines and on a body read whole (spec: openai-runner, "A credential never travels in the clear", "Every timeout the library applies is one of the runner's named settings", "A stream's lines are capped below the library"; openai-library design D2-D4a).

How the runner reaches a service through the openai package, against the fake endpoint: the credential only in a bearer Authorization header, no redirect followed, no retry by the library, no proxy for this machine, only the headers a request needs, and how errors, silences and cut streams come back (spec: openai-runner, "The credential goes only in the Authorization header", "A credential never travels in the clear", "Redirects are never followed", "Every timeout the library applies is one of the runner's named settings"; openai-library design D2-D4a).
plugins/runner-scripted/tests/test_scrip: Tests for the scripted runner, served in this process with troupe's messages already queued before it plays a step: steps after a result play before a waiting shutdown is answered, a waiting cancel is answered at the hang or wait it reaches or before a replay's delayed record, and a lone surrogate in a message is written as U+FFFD (spec: scripted-runner).
scripts/tests/test_check_parallel_unit.p: The tests gate's settings that run_gates relies on: the full and the scoped tests gates ask for the slowest tests' durations, and pyproject.toml sets a stall limit above the slowest test and within the CI job's room (spec: quality-check; parallel-tests design D1-D3; shorten-slow-tests design D4; windows-ci-hang design D1).
scripts/tests/test_check_scope_integrati: check.py's gates run for real: a scoped check passes when no tests were tagged and says so, the full check fails when no tests ran, and a failing gate stops the check and names itself, scoped or not (spec: quality-check; commit-check-paths design D8).
scripts/tests/test_flake_hunt_unit.py: How scripts/flake_hunt.py sets up its rounds, checked without running a hunt (spec: flake-hunt): --workers auto is three quarters of the usable CPUs less the load and at least one, a round's environment is the hunt's plus only its own Hypothesis directory, a round sets the stall limit only when the hunt is given one, and a log that isn't UTF-8 is shown escaped.
scripts/tests/workspace/test_install_che: The install check builds the documented command and keeps to its own directories (spec: installation; install-with-uv design D3 and D4; runner-extras design D9, D10). These tests check its parts without installing anything: the uv command and arguments for each kind of ref, with extras and --python, the tool directories and retry count it gives uv, a scratch directory removed even when a step fails, the version each ref expects, refusals of a tag whose pins or extras are wrong, and how it judges the version an install printed and each runner's refusal or rehearsal.

The install check's steps run for real: a ref resolves to its full commit or is refused by name, a failing or timed-out step is named with its command and output, and installs from a local index show the check's retry count outlasting failures that uv's default wouldn't (spec: installation; install-with-uv design D3 and D4).
scripts/tests/workspace/test_runner_lice:
Every package a runner plugin depends on is pinned in the lock and licensed compatibly with Apache-2.0, and a weak-copyleft one is only used unmodified, as its own package (spec: runner-protocol; runner-extras design D11, D13; owner, #333).

Each case builds a small workspace with a lock and fake installed metadata. The weak-copyleft notice is read from the list, never written here, so this file can't trip the copied-notice rule itself.
The licence check run on the real repository finds no problem: every package a runner plugin depends on has a listed licence (spec: runner-protocol; runner-extras design D11, D13; owner, #333).
